report.title: {Items.Count} antivirus {Plural(Items.Count, 'policy switches', 'policies switch')} unwanted application protection off

messages.businessImpact: Bundled software that is not malware but is not wanted either, browser toolbars, cryptocurrency miners and the installers that carry them, is allowed to install without objection. It is a support cost before it is a security one.
remediation: Set potentially unwanted application protection to Block.
Where it is in audit mode, review what it would have blocked first, since a genuine business tool occasionally trips it.
messages.cannotSee: Two settings switch this protection off, Defender's own and the SmartScreen one reached through the browser, and either being off is reported. Only a value this tool has read off a tenant is acted on, so an object that leaves the setting alone is not reported even though a device ends up the same. Where a security baseline or a configuration profile assigned in the same tenant switches the protection on, the object is passed over, because the device ends up protected whichever object did it. A Defender setting is read wherever it sits, whether that is an endpoint security policy, a security baseline or a Settings Catalog profile, and the report names which. An object that says nothing about a setting is not reported for it, because saying nothing and switching it off are different things and only the second is a finding.
